headline: ElevenLabs, the London-based AI voice company, says it will invest hundreds of millions of dollars in India and build a team of about 100 people there by the end of the year.
score_reason: On-the-record company plan reported by more than one outlet; the figures are company claims.
importance_line: ElevenLabs is putting India at the centre of its growth and training voice models on Indian languages, which matters to Indian developers and businesses, but the usage figures are the company's own.
summary: India Today reports, citing co-founder Mati Staniszewski's interview with CNBC-TV18 and a media briefing, that India is ElevenLabs' biggest market outside the US and that it will train voice models from the ground up on Indian languages, supporting 14 now and working to add 22 more. The company says it has worked with 250 enterprises there and that more than 25,000 developers and businesses use its API each month, up about 2.5 times in a year; these are company figures.
notes: Reuters page blocked; read India Today, which cites CNBC-TV18 and a media briefing. Reuters carried the same story (same headline in the pool). The figures are company claims.
